name: Torre BBVA (Castellana 81)
features: Dark steel-and-glass tower whose office floors are grouped in bands between recessed service levels.

photos.file: File:Fachada del edificio Castellana 81, AZCA, Madrid 1.jpg

note: Long known as the Banco de Bilbao tower. One of the chosen photos (Madrid Paseo de la Castellana-BBVA) is a fairly small 1882 x 3485 crop; a third photo shows the tower from below.

name: Fundació Pilar i Joan Miró, Moneo Building
features: Angular gallery with shallow pools on its roof and translucent stone skylights filtering light onto the art.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 1994 shortlist

photos.file: File:Fundació Pilar i Joan Miró Aussen 1.jpg

note: Year is the foundation's formal opening (1992, Wikipedia and the Commons infobox). Only two exterior photos of the Moneo building were found; most other files in the category show the gardens or Sert's studio, which is a separate entry here.

name: Joan Miró's Studio (Taller Sert)
features: Painter's studio under a row of wave-shaped concrete vaults that bring daylight deep into the workspace.

photos.file: File:Miro's Studio Sert - Palma de Mallorca.jpg

note: Year from the works list in Sert's Wikipedia article ("1955: Joan Miró studio"). Part of the same foundation grounds as the Moneo building.

name: Museum of the University of Navarra
features: Low, pale museum set into the green campus edge, its angular volumes holding galleries and a theatre.

photos.file: File:Museo de la Universidad de Navarra.jpg

note: Only one usable exterior photo on Commons (a distant view across the campus, 2412 x 1328). Commons gives an opening date of 22 January 2015; Moneo's Wikipedia list gives 2015.

name: La Muralla Roja
features: Kasbah-like block of cross-shaped towers in reds and pinks, linked by stairs, bridges and courtyards painted blue.
note: Bofill's Wikipedia article dates it 1968–1973.

name: Torres de Colón
features: Twin office towers whose floors hang from the tops of their concrete cores ("suspended architecture").
note: The chosen photos show the towers with the green 1990s crown. Commons also has categories for a refurbishment (Luis Vidal, 2020s) that changed the top; the owner may want a newer photo later.

name: Caja Granada Headquarters
features: Concrete cube with a deep gridded sunscreen facade; inside, a vast hall caught by skylights.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2003 shortlist

photos.file: File:Granada - Sede Central de Caja Granada 5.jpg
File:Granada - Sede Central de Caja Granada 2.jpg

name: Museum of Memory of Andalusia (MA)
features: Long white podium cut by an elliptical courtyard whose ramps spiral between the floors.
commons_category: Category:Centro Cultural CajaGranada Memoria de Andalucía

photos.file: File:Museo de Andalucía Fotógrafo- Javier Callejas.jpg

note: Two of the three photos show the open-air elliptical courtyard rather than the outer facade.

name: Royal Collections Gallery
by: Mansilla + Tuñón (Luis Moreno Mansilla, Emilio Tuñón)
features: Museum dug into the slope below the Royal Palace, its long facade a rhythm of pale vertical piers.

photos.file: File:Galeria de las Colecciones Reales - Madrid 02.jpg
File:Galeria de las Colecciones Reales - Madrid 03.jpg
File:Madrid - Galería de las Colecciones Reales.jpg

note: The Commons category also holds photos of the neighbouring Almudena Cathedral; only the gallery files were chosen.

name: Museu de Belles Arts de Castelló
features: Metal-clad gallery block whose stepped rooftop lanterns light the rooms, joined to an older building around a patio.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2001 shortlist
commons_category: Category:Museu de Belles Arts de Castelló

photos.file: File:Exterior del Museu de Belles Arts, Castelló de la Plana.JPG
File:Exterior del Museu de Belles Arts de Castelló.jpg
File:Museu de Belles Arts de Castelló, pati.jpg

note: Architect and opening date (25 January 2001) from the Commons/Wikidata infobox.

name: Auditorio Ciudad de León
features: White facade of deep, angled window boxes, each framing a different view of the city.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2003 shortlist

name: Woermann Tower
by: Ábalos & Herreros, with Joaquín Casariego and Elsa Guerra
features: 18-storey mixed-use tower and plaza, wrapped in a pixelated skin of green and yellow glass.
note: Two of the photos are from Panoramio (CC BY 3.0) and are about 2300 x 3072.

name: Usera Public Library (José Hierro)
features: Compact square tower of reading floors in grey cladding, with large framed windows looking over the park.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2003 shortlist
note: Only two free photos on Commons, both good exteriors.

name: Seville–Santa Justa Station
features: Brick station under a long curved concrete canopy, opening onto a high vaulted platform hall.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 1992 shortlist
note: Opened 2 May 1991 (Wikipedia); Cruz y Ortiz date the project 1987–1992. Also won the Spanish Architecture Award 1993.

name: Alamillo Bridge
features: A single leaning pylon, 142 m tall, balances the deck with its own weight, with no back-stay cables.

photos.file: File:Puente del Alamillo Guadalquivir Seville Spain.jpg

note: Built for Expo 92. Height from the Commons/Wikidata infobox.

name: La Ricarda (Casa Gomis)
features: Pavilion house of thin concrete vaults on a modular grid, spread among pine trees near the sea.

photos.file: File:01 La Ricarda (el Prat de Llobregat).jpg
File:02 La Ricarda (el Prat de Llobregat).jpg

note: Dated 1948–1963 in the Wikipedia article on Emilio Bofill (who built it). Commons has over 50 good free photos.

name: Badajoz Congress Centre (Manuel Rojas)
features: Circular drum wrapped in a skin of horizontal translucent tubes, with a red canopy at its entrance.

photos.file: File:Badajoz - Palacio de Congresos Manuel Rojas 1.jpg
File:Badajoz - Palacio de Congresos Manuel Rojas 2.jpg
File:Badajoz - Palacio de Congresos Manuel Rojas 4.jpg

name: El Batel Auditorium and Congress Centre
features: Long harbourfront auditorium of translucent coloured panels, with a public deck along the water.
commons_category: Category:Auditorio y Palacio de Congresos El Batel

photos.file: File:Auditorio y palacio de congresos El Batel (20240816 201251).jpg

note: Commons gives 2011 (inception) and an official opening on 15 March 2012.

name: Spanish Cultural Heritage Institute ("Corona de Espinas")
features: Ring of stacked concrete terraces around a round courtyard, crowned by spiky fins: the "Crown of Thorns".
commons_category: Category:Headquarters of the Cultural Heritage Institute of Spain, Madrid

photos.file: File:Inmueble del Instituto del Patrimonio Cultural de España, Madrid, desde el Faro de Moncloa.JPG

note: Designed 1967, built 1967–1970 (Wikipedia).

name: National Museum of Underwater Archaeology (ARQVA)
features: Low harbourside museum half sunk below a public plaza, with a long rust-coloured base and louvred upper band.

photos.file: File:Small people toward a modernist building in Cartagena in Spain - Holmstad 2016 AAA.jpg

note: Two of the photos come from a 2016 series titled "Modernist construction in Cartagena" (CC BY-SA 4.0) that is filed in the museum's category.

name: Trade Buildings
by: Josep Antoni Coderch and Manuel Valls
features: Four office towers with rippling glass curtain walls and no sharp corners, reflecting one another.
note: Year is the opening date on the Commons/Wikidata infobox; one Commons file title gives 1966–1968.

name: Jaume Fuster Library
features: Library whose broken, tilted roofs fold down towards Plaça de Lesseps, extending the square into the building.

photos.file: File:387 Biblioteca Jaume Fuster, pl. Lesseps 20 (Barcelona).jpg

note: Facts from Commons only: architect and inception (13 November 2005) from the Wikidata infobox; the FAD 2006 award from the titles of two files in the category. No English Wikipedia article.

name: CaixaForum Zaragoza
features: Two exhibition boxes lifted high on cantilevers, leaving the ground free as a shaded public square.

name: Pavilion of Knowledge (Pavilhão do Conhecimento)
features: White science museum around an open patio, its long upper block cantilevered over the court.
note: Built as the Knowledge of the Seas Pavilion for Expo 98; year is the Commons/Wikidata inception (25 July 1999). Photos are close views of the courtyard and canopy; no wide view of the whole building was found among the free files checked.

name: Nadir Afonso Contemporary Art Museum
features: Long white concrete museum lifted on piers above the riverside meadow.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2017 shortlist
commons_category: Category:Museu de Arte Contemporânea Nadir Afonso
note: Only two free exterior photos, both by Monade (CC BY-SA 4.0), very high resolution.

name: Setúbal School of Education
features: Low white school around a U-shaped lawn, lined by a deep colonnade.
commons_category: Category:Escola Superior de Educação do Instituto Politécnico de Setúbal
note: Dated 1986–1994 in a photo caption in Siza's Wikipedia article. A good interior (library) photo by Christian Gänshirt is also on Commons.

name: EDP Headquarters
by: Aires Mateus (Manuel and Francisco Aires Mateus)
features: Two blocks wrapped in dense white vertical fins that shade the glass, around a public passage to the river.
award: Secil Prize 2020; Mies van der Rohe Award 2017 shortlist

name: Amoreiras Towers
features: Postmodern office towers of pink and blue bands and mirror glass, with toy-like stepped tops.
note: Year from a photo caption in the Wikipedia article on postmodern architecture.

name: Church of Our Lady of the Rosary of Fátima
features: Early modern church with a slender bell tower, a carved entrance frieze and tall stained-glass windows.
commons_category: Category:Igreja de Nossa Senhora de Fátima (Lisbon)

photos.file: File:Igreja de Nossa Senhora de Fátima (Avenidas Novas - Lisboa).jpg
File:Igreja de Nossa Senhora de Fátima (Lisboa) 02.jpg
File:Igreja de Nossa Senhora do Rosário de Fátima (20442393640).jpg

name: Matosinhos Town Hall
features: Stone-clad town hall with long colonnades, set back behind a row of poplars on a civic square.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 1988 shortlist
note: Architect and opening date (8 December 1987) from the Commons/Wikidata infobox.

name: Cedro Primary School
features: Primary school of whitewashed wings and timber-lined covered play areas around open courtyards.

photos.file: File:Escola Primária Cedro exterior pormenor SilviaSantos.jpg
File:Recreio das meninas, vista geral em direção à entrada SílviaSantos.jpg

note: Year from the Commons/Wikidata label "Escola do Cedro (Gaia, 1958-60)"; Távora named as architect in the titles of files in the category. A set of 2020s photos by Silvia Santos documents the school well.

name: Coliseu do Porto
features: Streamlined theatre front with a stepped corner tower and a tall vertical sign.

photos.file: File:Coliseu do Porto, 29 de ourubro de 2016 (2).jpg

note: Opened 19 December 1941.

name: Metropolitano Stadium
features: Stadium built around a 1994 stand, now under a single tensile roof ring wrapping all four sides.
note: First built 1990–93 and opened 1994; rebuilt and reopened 2017, which is the form shown. Only one good exterior photo was chosen; the category also has many interior match photos that show the roof.

name: Universidad Laboral de Gijón
features: Vast stone-and-brick campus planned as a self-contained town around a colonnaded square and a tall tower.

photos.file: File:Gijón - Laboral Ciudad de la Cultura (ex Universidad Laboral) 02.jpg

note: Monumental classicising work of the Franco era, included as a precedent rather than as modernism; the owner may prefer to skip it.

name: Bilbao Metro entrances ("Fosteritos")
features: Curved glass shells that rise from the pavement over each metro stair, lit from within at night.
note: Foster won the station design competition in 1988; line 1 opened 11 November 1995.

name: Casa de la Marina (Barceloneta housing)
by: Josep Antoni Coderch and Manuel Valls
features: Slim corner block of flats behind full-height timber louvres, its plan bent to catch views and breeze.

photos.file: File:009 Habitatges Barceloneta, pg. Joan de Borbó.jpg

note: Coderch's Wikipedia list gives 1951 (the design); Commons file titles give 1952–1954 for construction. 1954 used.

name: Edificio Girasol
features: Apartment block whose saw-tooth facade turns every flat towards the sun ("girasol" means sunflower).

photos.file: File:Edificio Girasol Vista desde la esquina.jpg

note: Year is the Commons/Wikidata inception.

name: Bac de Roda Bridge
features: Calatrava's first bridge: paired, tilted steel arches carrying the road and footpaths over the railway.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 1988 shortlist
note: Built 1984–87 (Calatrava article). Several photos in the category are GFDL-only and were skipped.

name: National Museum and Research Center of Altamira
features: Low museum stepping along the hillside, its roofs folding into the slope; it houses a replica of the cave.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 2001 shortlist

photos.file: File:Museo Nacional y Centro de Interpretación de Altamira.jpg

note: Built 1995–2000 (Navarro Baldeweg article); official opening 17 July 2001 (Commons).

name: Castile and León Congress and Exhibition Centre
features: Sandstone block set against the old city wall, matching the golden stone of Salamanca.
award: Mies van der Rohe Award 1992 shortlist
commons_category: Category:Palacio de Congresos y Exposiciones de Castilla y León (Salamanca)
note: Dated 1985–1992 in Navarro Baldeweg's article. Few free photos: one street view (1280 x 934) and one city panorama in which it is prominent.

name: University of Deusto Library
features: Compact library block with chamfered corners, wrapped in glass behind a fine metal screen.
commons_category: Category:Biblioteca de la Universidad de Deusto

photos.file: File:Biblioteca de la Universidad de Deusto - Centro de Documentación Europea.jpg

name: Casa de las Flores
features: Brick apartment block around a garden courtyard, its terraces lined with flower boxes.
note: Wikipedia: designed 1931; a Commons file title gives 1930–32. Pablo Neruda lived here.

name: Casa Sindical
by: Francisco de Asís Cabrero and Rafael Aburto
features: Brick office slab with a strict grid of identical windows above a stone portico.

photos.file: File:Madrid - Casa Sindical (Ministerio de Sanidad, Política Social e Igualdad) 1.jpg
File:Ministerio De Sanidad, Politica Social E Igualdad (15905107331).jpg

note: Wikipedia gives 1951 as completion; Commons gives an official opening in 1955. Now the Ministry of Health.

name: Zubizuri
features: Curved footbridge hung from a single tilted steel arch over the river.

name: Xanadu
features: Seventeen flats stacked as cubes around a core, with tiled roof hoods, echoing the nearby Peñón de Ifach.
note: Only one free photo on Commons (CC0, a view through pines) and no Commons category. Dates differ: the Wikipedia article text says completed 1968, its infobox and Bofill's article say 1971 (1966–1971); 1971 used. A free plan exists (listed in extras).

name: La Fábrica
features: Old cement works carved into Bofill's home and studio: concrete silos with arched windows, overgrown with plants.
note: Converted from 1973, mostly completed 1975 (Wikipedia). Only two free photos (2022), both close views; no Commons category for the building found.
